old: But he had already shown part of his hand
new: But Porfiry had already shown part of his hand
reason: In a paragraph where 'he' alternates between Raskolnikov and Porfiry, the listener cannot tell at once who has shown his hand.

old: Amalia Ivanovna herself had been invited
new: Amalia Ivanovna -- Madame Lippevechsel -- herself had been invited
reason: The landlady is named as Madame Lippevechsel and then as Amalia Ivanovna a few sentences later, so a listener may take them for two different women.

old: That hateful, military, Pushkin expression is unthinkable
new: That hateful, military, Pushkin expression about a deceived husband's horns is unthinkable
reason: Luzhin never says 'horns' in this edition ('be made a fool of'), so the listener cannot tell which 'Pushkin expression' Lebeziatnikov is attacking.

old: always walked with his hands in his pockets
new: always went with hands in pockets
reason: Katerina Ivanovna then mocks this phrasing as meaning 'hands in people's pockets', so Amalia's broken wording needs to be ambiguous for the joke to work.

old: but she said he put his hands in people's pockets
new: but the way she said it, it sounds as if he put his hands in other people's pockets
reason: As written, it seems to contradict what Amalia was just quoted as saying. This makes clear that the joke is about how her phrasing sounds.
Amalia mixes in German words (Vater, die Wäsche), and 'gold' sounds like an error for German 'Geld', meaning money.

new: As if you would take it! How stupid
reason: Said straight after 'I don't believe it!', the line sounds like Katerina Ivanovna accusing Sonia, which is the opposite of what she means.
The previous chapter calls it 'the yellow ticket', so the same period term should be used here.

old: I didn't know he was staying here in your room, and so on that very same day
new: I didn't know he was staying here in your room, and so I didn't know that on that very same day
reason: As written, 'and so' makes Luzhin's seeing the money follow from Raskolnikov's not knowing, which is illogical. The point is that Raskolnikov did not know he had been seen.

old: in my room! Get out at once,
new: in my room!" cried Lebeziatnikov. "Get out at once,
reason: The line comes straight after a speech by Luzhin with no speaker named, so a listener cannot tell that Lebeziatnikov is now speaking.
